standard_prerequisites.name: Ordinal
standard_prerequisites.statement: An ordinal is a set that is transitive and well-ordered by membership.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof uses transitivity of alpha at source lines 421-422 and 425-427, and well-orderedness of alpha where it invokes the retained proposition (source line 428-430).

standard_prerequisites.name: Transitive set
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set b is transitive when c in b implies c subseteq b.
standard_prerequisites.use: The second half of the proof proves exactly that b is transitive, starting from x in c in b (source lines 425-431).

standard_prerequisites.name: Membership is a strict well-order on an ordinal
standard_prerequisites.statement: On an ordinal alpha the membership relation is irreflexive, asymmetric and transitive, and every non-empty subset of alpha has a unique least element (the retained context proposition wo:strictorder).
standard_prerequisites.use: The transitivity clause is applied to x, c, b in alpha at source lines 427-430.

core_obligations: Show that membership well-orders b: from b in alpha and the transitivity of alpha obtain b subseteq alpha, and inherit the well-ordering of alpha by membership (source lines 421-423).

Show that b is transitive: given x in c in b, use b subseteq alpha and the transitivity of alpha twice to place x, c, b in alpha, then apply the transitivity of membership on alpha from the retained proposition to conclude x in b, and generalise to c subseteq b (source lines 425-431).

proof_roadmap.step: From b in alpha and transitivity of alpha get b subseteq alpha, hence membership well-orders b.
Given x in c in b, move into alpha twice using b subseteq alpha and transitivity of alpha.
Apply transitivity of membership on alpha (retained proposition wo:strictorder) to x in c in b, conclude x in b and generalise to c subseteq b.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma ordmemberord at source lines 416-418: every element of an ordinal is an ordinal. The proof at source lines 420-431 has to establish two independent clauses for b in alpha: that b is well-ordered by membership (which is inherited from alpha, using that alpha is transitive) and that b is transitive. The second clause is where the work lies: from x in c in b one must push c into alpha using b subseteq alpha, then push x into alpha using the transitivity of alpha, and only then apply the fact that membership is a transitive relation on alpha — so the proof needs the transitivity clause of the author's proposition wo:strictorder, which is stated far away in the well-orderings section. Because that proposition is invoked by its source label, its statement and proof are retained as context so the reference resolves inside the assembled package. The argument is elementary but both steps must be found; nothing outside the retained text is used.

ordissetofsmallerord (statement 433-436, proof 438-440) is the corollary that alpha equals the set of its elements which are ordinals, and it cites our counted lemma ordmemberord; it is a different proposition and our card does not count the corollary.
